components.role: initiates instruction/data/MMIO transactions and consumes interrupts
decodes CPU requests to RAM and peripheral IP regions
updates time/status and raises timer interrupt
maps external GPIO pins to status and interrupt-like events

dependency_rules.name: address_decode_selects_target_ip
dependency_rules.baseline: Address bits are directly sliced and each IP input can still toggle independently.
dependency_rules.depaware: A raw region selector chooses RAM/UART/MTIMER/GPIO/SPI, then projected address bits are placed inside the selected region.
dependency_rules.source: RVX documented address map in candidate component notes.

dependency_rules.name: request_response_progress
dependency_rules.baseline: Request, ready, valid, response and data are independent bit slices.
dependency_rules.depaware: Response valid is only asserted for a selected transaction; ready/valid are biased toward progress while still controlled by raw bits.

dependency_rules.name: timer_status_drives_timer_irq
dependency_rules.baseline: Timer IRQ is an independent bit slice.
dependency_rules.depaware: Timer IRQ is gated by timer event/status raw fields and can be cleared by a projected MMIO write.

dependency_rules.name: peripheral_status_drives_external_irq
dependency_rules.baseline: GPIO/UART/SPI IRQs are independent bit slices.
dependency_rules.depaware: External IRQ is derived from selected peripheral event/status fields with low-frequency gate and priority.
dependency_rules.source: GPIO/UART/SPI status and interrupt style semantics.

dependency_rules.name: error_debug_priority
dependency_rules.baseline: Error, debug and IRQ bits can all toggle independently and densely.
dependency_rules.depaware: Error/debug/IRQ use raw-controlled low-frequency gates and a fixed priority to avoid every-cycle domination.

fairness.notes: Baseline and depaware differ only in how rfuzz_input_bits are interpreted by the harness. Both must drive the same composite target and use the same coverage port.
